To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found a new class of analytic constants beyond the multiple polylogarithms and the generalized harmonic sums and that we have developed a computer algebra toolbox that is able to calculate these constants.

the three loop massive operator matrix elements are expressible in terms nested sums, that these can be computed with the help of computer algebra, that they form a quasi shuffle algebra, and that they lead to a plethora of new constants.
all three loop ladder and three loop V topology objects can be expressed in terms nested sums and recursions depending on the Melln variable and the dimensional parameter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods in the area of computer algebra.
the analytic continuation of the Laurent expansion of the three loop massive operator matrix element.
the calculation of the three loop ladder and the three loop V topologies for the massive operator matrix elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calculation of three loop ladder and massive V topology diagrams is possible in principle.
we are able to compute the three loop massive operator matrix element to any desired accuracy in terms of nested harmonic sums.
the three loop ladder and the V topology diagrams contributing A Q g are completely determined by our results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a complete computer algebra system for the calculation of three loop ladder and three loop V topology diagrams.
the three loop ladder and the V topologies are the first cases where we can obtain the complete Laurent expansion for the massive operator matrix elements.
we can calculate the three loop massive operator matrix elements A Q g and A Q g up to weight 6, and A Q g and the corresponding master integrals up to weight 5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calculation of Laurent series solutions for coupled systems of differential equation with symbolic parameters is possible in a completely automated way.
the calculation of Laurent series expansions of Feynman integrals in dimensional regularization can be performed in a fully automatic fashion.
the computer algebra toolbox is now able to deal with the full complexity of the three loop ladder and the V topologies.
